title: Facial Orthography Boundary
subtitle: Why official Unicode SignWriting is not a production basis for facial writing
summary: A production-first boundary note: the official Unicode SignWriting block is a Unicode-scoped character-encoding artifact, not the Sutton SignWriting production symbol repertoire, production text model, or production basis for complete written signs.
synopsis: This practitioner guide helps readers choose Sutton SignWriting text models, tools, corpora, datasets, archives, publications, education, and AI workflows. It evaluates official Unicode by the production function people are likely to assign to it, rather than by whether Unicode or UTC promised a complete production text model. The boundary is direct: Sutton SignWriting production text must preserve the authored written sign; for facial writing, that includes selected Sutton SignWriting facial symbols and authored arrangement. Official Unicode facial writing stores U+1D9FF SIGNWRITING HEAD plus nonspacing facial marks, so missing authored arrangement cannot be recovered and official Unicode SignWriting should not be used as the production basis for Sutton SignWriting facial writing. The note explains that preserving authored facial arrangement keeps evidence available for community orthographic development without declaring every placement difference canonical, and that reliable interchange matters in AI, machine-learning, corpus, and dataset workflows. It separates text-model requirements from rendering: complete written signs are text elements, authored spatial layout is plain-text content, serialization is not linearization, and coordinates or equivalent spatial relations belong in the production text model and serialization, not necessarily in ordinary Unicode coordinate characters. It also addresses standards and implementation objections: notation-style classification confirms the boundary; Unicode has a preservation mismatch around spatial spelling and higher-level scope; FSW/SWU-based workflows treat complete written signs as language text units; and MusicXML analogies, added coordinates, better fonts, Unicode-native authoring, conformance tests, and implementation claims do not repair the official facial sequence. Production work should use FSW/SWU, Sutton SignWriting-compatible tooling, or an equivalent coordinate-preserving model.

primary_artifact.cover_summary: Production text for Sutton SignWriting must preserve the written sign the author composed. For facial writing, that includes selected facial symbols and authored arrangement. Official Unicode stores a head plus nonspacing facial marks, leaving facial construction to rendering. This note explains why that model is a Unicode-scoped artifact, not a production basis for complete Sutton SignWriting signs.

companion_documents.cover_summary: Matrix of production requirements, official Unicode behavior, and resulting risks for Sutton SignWriting facial writing. It shows where the head-plus-mark model loses authored facial arrangement and why added coordinates, fonts, conformance tests, or implementation claims do not repair that loss.

companion_documents.label: Production Warning
companion_documents.cover_summary: Short production warning for implementers, archivists, educators, publishers, and dataset builders: do not route Sutton SignWriting production work through the official Unicode facial model. Use FSW/SWU or an equivalent coordinate-preserving model that preserves selected symbols, sign boundaries, and authored facial arrangement.

slides.title: Verdict
slides.summary: The official Unicode SignWriting block should not be used as the basis for Sutton SignWriting production text.

slides.speech: The verdict is direct. The official Unicode SignWriting block should not be used as the basis for Sutton SignWriting production text. The official Unicode block is a Unicode-scoped character-encoding artifact. It is not the Sutton SignWriting production symbol repertoire, not the Sutton SignWriting production text model, and not a production foundation for complete written signs. The facial-diacritic model is the decisive failure point.
slides.notes: Open with the production requirement rather than with institutional status.

slides.title: Production Requirement
slides.summary: Sutton SignWriting production facial writing must preserve selected symbols and authored spatial relations.

bullets: Writers select Sutton SignWriting facial symbols
slides.speech: The production requirement comes first. Sutton SignWriting production text must preserve the written sign the author composed. For facial writing, that means preserving the Sutton SignWriting facial symbols the writer selected and the authored facial arrangement. ISWA 2010 remains the Sutton SignWriting production symbol repertoire. FSW/SWU preserve selected ISWA 2010 symbols and authored spatial relations in the working Sutton SignWriting ecosystem. Other production models are possible only if they preserve the same necessary data.
slides.notes: Make Unicode answer to the production requirement, not the other way around.

slides.title: Different Model
slides.summary: HEAD plus facial marks is not a partial Sutton SignWriting production model; it is a different model.

image_prompts.concrete: A Unicode HEAD plus mark sequence contrasted with an authored Sutton SignWriting facial composition
image_prompts.abstract: A component list collapsing authored spatial composition

slides.speech: The official facial-diacritic model is the decisive failure point. It represents facial writing as U+1D9FF SIGNWRITING HEAD plus nonspacing facial marks. That is not a partial version of Sutton SignWriting production facial writing. It is a different model. It stores a head plus component categories and asks the renderer to construct the face. It does not store the Sutton SignWriting facial symbols the writer selected or the authored facial arrangement.

slides.title: No Rescue
slides.summary: A higher-level production model may preserve SignWriting, but that does not rescue the official Unicode block as the basis.

bullets: Then production model is the basis
Unicode marks are not independent symbols
slides.speech: A higher-level production model may preserve Sutton SignWriting. That does not rescue the official Unicode block as a production basis. If a model preserves ISWA 2010 identity, selected symbols, authored coordinates, sign boundaries, and authored facial arrangement, then that model is the basis. The common escape route is to say that Unicode can be the symbol layer and a higher-level protocol can add coordinates. That fails for facial writing because signbox coordinates cannot reach inside a font-constructed face, and coordinates cannot recover production data the sequence never stored.
slides.notes: Answer the most persistent misunderstanding directly.

slides.title: Not The Path
slides.summary: A conformance suite can prove failure, but it cannot prove future adequacy for a living orthography.

image_prompts.concrete: A checklist proving selected failures beside a living SignWriting community developing new facial forms
image_prompts.abstract: A test suite too small for future orthographic development

bullets: Passing tests cannot prove future adequacy
Do not spend scarce effort rescuing the model
State the boundary and build forward
slides.speech: A conformance suite may be useful for researchers, implementers, or critics who want to demonstrate particular failures of the official Unicode facial model. It is not the correct practical path for Sutton SignWriting production communities. A suite can show failure. It cannot prove that the model is adequate for a living writing system whose future community distinctions, local practices, poetic uses, pedagogical forms, and complex facial arrangements may develop over time.
slides.notes: Prevent the build a loss-audit suite recommendation from becoming the agenda.

slides.title: Common Misreadings
slides.summary: The official Unicode block is not the symbol layer, citation layer, or text foundation for Sutton SignWriting production text.

image_prompts.concrete: A set of misconception cards crossed out beside the correct production path through FSW and SWU
image_prompts.abstract: Wrong paths closed off by a production-first boundary

slides.speech: The common misreadings are predictable. Unicode cannot be treated as the symbol layer with FSW as the layout layer for production facial writing. A higher-level protocol cannot restore production facial authorship that the official sequence never stored. Unicode character citation is not production symbol citation. Official Unicode support does not mean production Unicode support. The practical path is to route production work around the official Unicode facial model.
slides.notes: Close by removing the escape routes.
